**Statement.** Let k be any field and let a,b in k[G] satisfy ab=1 but ba != 1. For any t in supp(b), put b'=b t^{-1} and a'=t a; let H_b be the subgroup generated by supp(b'). Then k[H_b] itself contains a one-sided inverse pair c,b' with c b'=1 but b' c !=1. Dually, for any t in supp(a), set a'=t^{-1}a, b'=b t, H_a=<supp(a')>; there exists d in k[H_a] with a'd=1 but d a' !=1. Consequently, each of H_a and H_b is nonsofic and nonamenable (using sofic direct finiteness and amenable => sofic), irrespective of what the rest of G does.

**Proof for b.** Both a'b'=1 and b'a'=ba !=1. Decompose k[G] as the direct sum of the left-coset subspaces u k[H_b]. Right multiplication by b' preserves each summand, and 1 lies in the identity summand k[H_b]. Let c be the k[H_b]-component of a'. Projecting a'b'=1 gives c b'=1. If b' c=1, then a'=a'(b'c)=(a'b')c=c, yielding b'a'=1, contradiction. Hence b'c !=1.

**Proof for a.** Here a'b'=1 and b'a'=ba !=1. Decompose k[G] as direct sum of right-coset subspaces k[H_a]u. Left multiplication by a' preserves them. Let d be the k[H_a]-component of b'. Then a'd=1. If d a'=1, then b'=(d a')b'=d(a'b')=d, hence b'a'=1, contradiction. QED.

This is a **support-localization**, stronger than merely generating a witness subgroup from supp(a) union supp(b). It is an elementary coset-projection argument and may be implicit in published cellular-automaton subgroup-restriction results. It is **not** certified as new to the wider literature. For family-197 it applies to the *original* group and its particular a,b, without changing the group.

**Corollary 1 (uniform single-support expansion).** For k=F_2, fix t in S_b=supp(b) and set K=S_b t^{-1}, so 1 in K and H_b=<K> nonamenable. There is an epsilon_b>0 depending only on K such that every nonempty finite T subset G obeys

    |T S_b| = |T K| >= (1+epsilon_b)|T|.

To prove existence, if there were finite nonempty F_n subset H_b with |F_n K|/|F_n| -> 1, then because 1 in K, for each k in K we have |F_n triangle F_n k| <= 2(|F_n K|-|F_n|)=o(|F_n|). The same asymptotic holds for k^-1 and products, producing a right Folner sequence for the finitely generated group H_b, contradicting nonamenability. For arbitrary T subset G, partition T into left H_b-cosets and apply the H_b inequality in each coset; summing yields the claim. # Corrected research audit: direct finiteness, Bernoulli isomorphism, and positive characteristic

Date: 2026-10-08 (Brisbane). Independent proof audit using original OpenAI family-197 source, Seward's original theorems, Formanek 1973, Burger–Valette, and Bartels–Lück–Reich.

**Research status.** Algebraic deductions below are proved **conditional on** an explicit non-direct-finiteness witness in a countably infinite group algebra. Entropy statements use published Seward theorems exactly as quoted. Family-197's entire probabilistic/topological construction and the separate N129 hyperbolic strengthening have NOT been independently certified; no explicit matching/finite presentation was acquired. Historical priority and peer review remain unknown. The full Bernoulli isomorphism question is NOT settled.

**This supersedes the disputed claims in** state/2026-10-08-bowen-bernoulli-direct-finiteness/RESEARCH.md, ADDITIONAL_AUDITS.md, state/2026-10-08-formanek-frontier/RESEARCH_STATE.md, the group-theory Section B of state/2026-10-08-full-proofs-and-audits.md, and the main index's "Formanek impossibility" gloss. The unrelated mathematical claims in those records are not being retracted by this focused audit.

## 1. Explicit input and scope

Assume G is countably infinite; q is a prime power; R=F_q[G]; a,b in R with ab=1 but ba!=1. Set r=1-ba, S=supp(r), m=|S|. Then r is a nonzero proper idempotent (r^2=r); r=1 would imply ba=0 and a=aba=0, contradicting ab=1. In particular m>=2: a nonzero one-term idempotent in a group algebra is 1.

The released OpenAI family-197 torsion-free preprint, at
https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Group-Algebra-That-Is-Not-Directly-Finite-October-4-2026/build/sections ,
asserts finite presentation, torsion-freeness, a finite 2-dimensional classifying complex, and a,b,c in F_2[G] with ab=1, ac=0, c!=0. The parity-criterion calculation can be checked algebraically in algebra.tex. The global graph exclusion / cone picture / topology / random-selection arguments are nontrivial and were NOT fully independently established by this audit. No numerical m or concrete words for a,b were acquired; the selection is existential.
